sections.normalized_html: An archer shoots an arrow straight upward. The graph shown models the arrow’s height above the ground, [MATH: y], in meters, [MATH: x] seconds after release. What is the intervals of time was the arrow falling throughout the entire interval?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/d495cce626f445a16198e8dd13361e8e]

An archer shoots an arrow straight upward. The graph shown models the arrow’s height above the ground, [MATH: y], in meters, [MATH: x] seconds after release. What is the intervals of time was the arrow falling throughout the entire interval?

sections.normalized_html:
We want to find when the height was decreasing continuously. The graph is a downward-opening parabola with a vertex at [MATH: x=2.8] seconds.

The arrow rises until the peak at [MATH: x=2.8,] then descends. So, it was falling continuously for [MATH: 2.8\le x\le 5.2.]

Among the given choices, the only interval lying entirely within this falling section is [MATH: \text{From } x = 3 \text{ to } x = 5.]

The graph shows the number of subscribers, [MATH: y], in thousands, [MATH: x] months after a new series premiered, where [MATH: 0 \le x \le 5.] What is the best describes the increase in subscribers from [MATH: x = 0] to [MATH: x = 3?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/73f5dfd82b16dccc793c1ed6e577cefe]

A streaming platform tracks its subscriber count. The graph shows the number of subscribers, [MATH: y], in thousands, [MATH: x] months after a new series premiered, where [MATH: 0 \le x \le 5.] What is the best describes the increase in subscribers from [MATH: x = 0] to [MATH: x = 3?]

sections.normalized_html:
From the graph, we have:

  • At [MATH: x = 0{:}] the number of subscribers is [MATH: 3] thousands.

  • At [MATH: x = 3{:}] the number of subscribers is approximately [MATH: 9] thousands.

To find how many times larger the value at [MATH: x = 3] is compared to [MATH: x = 0,] we divide the number of subscribers at [MATH: x = 3] by the number at [MATH: x = 0{:}] [MATH: \frac{9{,}000}{3{,}000} = 3]

Therefore, the best interpretation that describes the increase from [MATH: x = 0] to [MATH: x = 3] is the following:

The number of subscribers at [MATH: x = 3] is [MATH: 3] times the number at [MATH: x = 0.]

> The number of subscribers at [MATH: x = 3] is [MATH: 3] times the number at [MATH: x = 0.]
